reply: For a pilot you can start with NIR transmission on the clear whey and NIR diffuse‑reflection on the opaque milk concentrate, then run a side‑by‑side comparison against your lab protein/fat results.

report.title: Pilot measurement concepts for whey and milk concentrate

answer.text: It depends on the optical appearance of each stream; NIR transmission is most suitable for the clear whey, while NIR diffuse‑reflection is the most promising first candidate for the opaque milk concentrate.

concept.summary: Install a transmission NIR probe in the whey line (pathlength 1–5 mm) and a diffuse‑reflection NIR probe in the milk concentrate line (flush‑mounted to the pipe wall). Use the same spectrometer platform (e.g., FT‑NIR or diode‑array) to acquire spectra, apply chemometric calibration (PLS) against lab protein/fat measurements, and compare model performance for each interface.

concept.fiberLink: Standard silica fiber (low‑OD) suitable for NIR transmission
concept.analyzer: NIR spectrometer (FT‑NIR or DAD‑based) capable of both transmission and reflectance modes

risks: Insufficient transmission for whey if pathlength is too long, leading to signal loss.
Surface sensitivity of reflection may cause variability if fat globule size changes.
Potential fouling of probes in the concentrate stream; cleaning strategy needed.

steps: Collect representative whey and concentrate samples covering expected protein/fat ranges.
Measure each sample with the transmission probe (whey) and reflection probe (concentrate) using the same NIR spectrometer.
Obtain reference protein and fat values from the laboratory methods.
Build separate PLS calibration models for each probe, validate on held‑out samples.
Then measure in-line or in a pilot set-up against the reference method.
Compare prediction errors and robustness; decide which interface meets the pilot criteria.
feasibility.decisionBasis: Model validation statistics (RMSEP, bias) agreed with the customer before testing; the simplest probe that meets the required accuracy will be selected. Agree two things separately with the customer before the test: the model accuracy required against the reference method, and the alarm or action threshold applied to the measured value.
